Title: Document 5
Content: `text(One)` of the worst times was the fasting month of Ramadan in `2008`. During Ramadan no food or drink can pass a Muslim’s lips in daylight `text(hours)`. The Taliban bombed the power station, so we had no electricity, then a few `text(days)` later they blasted the pipeline, so we had no gas either. The price of the gas cylinders we used to buy from the market `text(doubled)`, so my mother had to cook on a fire like we did in the village. She didn’t complain — food needed to be cooked and she cooked it, and there were others worse off than us. But there was no clean water and people started dying from cholera. The hospital could not cope with all the patients and had to erect big tents outside to treat people.

Though we had no generator at home, my father bought `text(one)` to install at the school, and fresh water was pumped from a borehole, which all the children in the neighborhood went to collect. Every `text(day)` there would be lines of people waiting to fill jugs, bottles and drums. `text(One)` of the neighbors got frightened. “What are you doing?” he asked. “If the Taliban find out you’re giving water in the month of Ramadan they will bomb us!”
My father replied that people would die either of thirst or bombings. . . .
